feature_request: We need a better way to track who is the right person to contact in each country.

proposed_scope_in.item: Country page 'Who to contact' panel: shows 1 recommended contact plus up to 2 alternates, each with a one-line reason generated from the rule that ranked it (e.g. 'Lead on active mission; last engaged 12 days ago'), and the contact's details.

Deterministic ranking rules over existing Country, Contact, Mission, Project and Engagement data. Order: (1) linked to the selected active mission or project; (2) role priority from the existing contact role field; (3) most recent engagement; (4) has at least one valid contact method. Ties break on most recent engagement, then alphabetically, so results are reproducible.

Optional context selector on the panel: choose an active Mission or Project for that country to re-rank. Default is country-level. The selector uses existing Mission and Project records, with no new topic taxonomy.

Last-engaged date and a computed 'possibly stale' badge when a contact has no engagement in the last 180 days. Both are derived from the existing Engagement history, so coordinators enter nothing new.
Computed 'missing contact method' indicator on contacts lacking email and phone, shown inline in the panel only.
Fallback behaviour: if no contact qualifies, show 'No recommended contact' and the country's full existing contact list, rather than guessing.
Panel and rankings inherit the existing Country/Mission access model. Users see only contacts they can already see, and no new permission types are added.

proposed_scope_out: Manual 'primary contact' designation fields or any new data-entry step for Regional Coordinators
New tables or entities (e.g. a ContactRole, Topic or Preference table); v1 uses computed queries over existing entities
ML or scoring models; ranking is fixed, explainable rules
Contact verification or confirmation workflows, approval steps, or review queues
Notifications, alerts, or dashboards for stale contacts
Per-country configuration or settings for ranking rules or staleness thresholds
Availability, out-of-office, time-zone, or language-preference handling
External directory sync, bulk import, or deduplication tooling
Protocol, precedence, or seniority rules between officials, and security clearance or data classification handling; these are policy decisions for humans, not product design
Cross-country search or 'who handles topic X across all countries' views

assumptions.statement: 'Right person' means the best current contact for a given country, optionally narrowed to a mission or project; it is not a global directory or a per-topic expertise map.
assumptions.rationale: Keeps the question answerable with existing Country, Mission and Project links. A topic or expertise taxonomy would require a new schema and ongoing maintenance.

assumptions.statement: The existing Contact role, contact-detail and Engagement data is complete enough to rank contacts with simple deterministic rules, without any new fields being filled in.
assumptions.rationale: Zero extra data entry for Regional Coordinators means the feature must work from data already captured, and fixed rules are cheap to build, test and explain. The fallback and missing-detail indicator cover gaps.

assumptions.statement: Recent engagement history is a good-enough proxy for whether a contact is still current and reachable; a 180-day silence is a reasonable 'possibly stale' signal.
assumptions.rationale: Staleness can be computed automatically from logging coordinators already do. A fixed default threshold avoids per-country settings, and the badge is advisory only.

assumptions.statement: Existing Country/Mission access controls already determine who may see which contacts, so the new panel needs no separate permission model.
assumptions.rationale: Reusing current access rules avoids building RBAC and avoids creating a new data-exposure surface. The panel only re-presents data the user can already view.

assumptions.statement: Mission and Project affiliation, as already recorded on contacts, is the only context needed to tailor the recommendation in v1.
assumptions.rationale: Those links already exist, so context-aware ranking costs a query filter rather than a new entity or taxonomy.

success_criteria: At launch, on existing data, at least 90% of the ~100 countries show a recommended contact with at least one valid contact method (measured by a query).
Zero new required fields or data-entry steps for Regional Coordinators, and zero new database tables in v1.
In a 10-country pilot review of 50 sampled lookups, at least 80% of recommended contacts are judged correct or acceptable by the responsible Regional Coordinator.
The panel loads in under 2 seconds at p95, and a user reaches a recommended contact within 2 clicks from the country page.
Every recommendation displays a human-readable reason, and 100% of rankings are reproducible: identical data yields identical output.
The v1 feature ships within a single release cycle.

challenges.challenge_text: Staleness is inferred from engagement recency, but turnover (minister reshuffle, ministry staff departure, our coordinator leaving) is not the same as silence. A contact who left office yesterday but was engaged 12 days ago is ranked first with a 'Lead on active mission; last engaged 12 days ago' reason and no stale badge, so a coordinator confidently calls or emails a departed official or sends sensitive material to the wrong ministry person. Conversely, a correct contact in a low-frequency relationship (say, a country with 1-2 engagements a year) gets flagged 'possibly stale' after 180 days. Across 100 countries most contacts get the badge, and people learn to ignore it. Recency also rewards whoever was logged most often, not who currently holds the role. The proposal has no signal for 'role ended' or 'recently confirmed', and the UI presents the result as authoritative.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: No responses yet in Round 1. The 'advisory only' framing doesn't address that the top recommendation carries an authoritative reason string while the data it relies on cannot detect departure.

challenges.challenge_text: The panel claims to inherit the existing Country/Mission access model, but it does something new: it ranks and generates reasons from Engagement history, mission links and last-engaged dates. A user with Country access but not Mission access could infer the existence of a confidential mission, or see a reason string like 'Lead on active mission X; last engaged 12 days ago', when engagement notes or mission membership are restricted. The context selector lists Missions and Projects per country, and may reveal missions the user is not on. Ranking over contacts they can see can still disclose hidden data through the derived 'reason' text, the alternates, or the fact that a restricted contact is skipped. It is also unverified that existing access is actually enforced at contact, engagement and mission level, rather than at country level only. Least privilege may be broken at the aggregation layer, not at the row layer.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1: A4 is asserted without evidence that Mission, Engagement and Contact visibility are enforced per record, nor that the ranking query runs with the viewer's permissions rather than service-level access.

challenges.challenge_text: The claim that existing Contact role, detail and Engagement data is 'complete enough' is unvalidated. Role is likely free text or an inconsistent field across 100 countries (e.g. 'Minister', 'Ministre', 'Focal Point', blank). 'Role priority from the existing role field' then ranks arbitrarily or misorders, such as a junior desk officer ahead of the Director. Duplicate contacts, or contacts never logged in Engagement, are ranked low or never. 'Has a valid contact method' is only presence, not validity, so a bounced email or disconnected number counts as valid. The 90% success metric measures only that some contact with a method exists, not that it is correct, which allows a high-looking launch with wrong recommendations. The 80% pilot threshold means 1 in 5 may be wrong, and a wrong ministry contact is a diplomatic incident, not a mere inconvenience.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1: Proposer has no data-quality audit, no role normalization or mapping, and a launch metric that does not measure correctness.

challenges.challenge_text: Returning exactly one 'recommended' contact plus two alternates implies a single right answer, but in practice sensitive outreach often needs the contact for a specific purpose, and a lead on one mission may be the wrong person for a different topic. Default country-level view ranks by mission link or recent engagement, so a coordinator opening the page without selecting context gets the contact for whichever mission is most active. They then reach out to that person about an unrelated or sensitive matter. Also, if the recommended contact was tied to a mission the viewer cannot see, the reason line becomes misleading. A one-line reason that looks authoritative will be trusted without checking.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1: A1 limits scope to country/mission, but nothing mitigates misuse of the default country-level recommendation for out-of-scope topics, such as a prominent disclaimer or showing the ranking basis.

proposed_scope_in.item: Country page 'Who to contact' panel: 1 suggested first contact plus up to 2 alternates. Each shows its details, the contact's role exactly as recorded, the last-engaged date, and a one-line ranking basis. A fixed header reads 'Country-level default, not topic-specific. Select a mission or project to narrow.' Reasons are built only from records the viewer can see.

Deterministic ranking over existing Country, Contact, Mission, Project and Engagement data. Order: (1) linked to the mission or project the user selected; this step is skipped at country level, so the default view never ranks by whichever mission is most active; (2) role priority, applied only to role values in an existing controlled list, with free-text or blank roles skipped at this step; (3) most recent engagement; (4) has a contact method on file. Ties break on most recent engagement, then alphabetically.
Optional context selector listing only the active Missions and Projects for that country that the viewer is already permitted to see. It uses existing records and has no new topic taxonomy.

Neutral last-engaged date with a fixed label 'Engagement date does not confirm the person still holds this role'. The 180-day 'possibly stale' badge is removed because it is noisy and could be misread as validation.

Exclude from recommendations, and show as 'marked inactive', any contact already flagged inactive or ended on the existing Contact record. This is a rule over existing data. If no such field exists, it is a no-op and no field is added.
Computed 'no contact method on file' indicator for contacts lacking email and phone, shown inline in the panel only. The wording says 'on file', not 'valid'.
Fallback: if no contact qualifies, show 'No recommended contact' and the country's full existing contact list, rather than guessing.

Panel queries run under the viewing user's existing Country/Mission/Contact/Engagement permissions, not service-level access. Any reason clause, alternate, or selector entry that depends on a record the viewer cannot see is omitted. No new permission types are added.

Pre-launch read-only data-quality audit query (not a user feature) reporting the share of contacts with a controlled role, with a contact method, and with at least one engagement, per country. It is a release gate: if role coverage is too low in a country, the role-priority step is not trusted there and the panel falls back to the full list.

challenge_responses.response: The Critic is right that engagement recency cannot detect departure and that a 180-day badge across ~100 low-frequency relationships would be noisy and ignored. Fix is cheap and removes scope: drop the day-threshold badge, show the last-engaged date with a fixed label that it does not confirm the current role, and exclude contacts already marked inactive on the existing record (no field is added; it is a no-op if none exists). A3 is reworded to match. I am not adding a 'last confirmed' field, verification workflow, or turnover tracker. Those need coordinator data entry or a monitored queue, which breaks the zero-friction goal. The residual risk is a departed official with no inactive flag who was recently engaged. The pilot criterion of zero known-departed suggestions measures it, and the neutral label bounds it. Evidence for a later automated 'role ended' field: pilot misses traced to departures, or more than a few per cent of the sampled lookups.

The aggregation-layer leak is real, but the fix is a constraint on the query, not a new feature. The panel runs under the viewer's own permissions. Reason text, alternates and selector entries are built only from records the viewer can see. Anything depending on an invisible mission or engagement is omitted, and the country-level default no longer uses mission links for ranking, so no mission name reaches the reason line. An automated test (user with Country but not Mission access) is a release criterion. A4 stays word-for-word because this is how it is honoured. Whether existing access is enforced per record or only per country is a fact I cannot verify from here. If it is country-level only, whether mission or engagement details may be shown to those users is a security/data-classification decision for a human owner, and I will not invent a policy. In that case the panel would show only contact details and role, with no mission-derived reasons.

I accept most of this where the fix is a rule or query. Changes: role priority applies only to values in an existing controlled list, so free-text or blank roles do not misorder results. The recorded role text is shown so the coordinator can judge. 'Valid' contact method is relabelled 'on file', because presence is all we can claim. The 90% launch metric is relabelled as coverage and a separate correctness criterion is added, with the pilot threshold raised from 80% to 90% and every miss root-caused. A read-only pre-launch audit query is a release gate, and the panel falls back to the full contact list where role data is too thin. I defend against the other fixes: role normalization or mapping tables, deduplication, and bounce or number validation are new tables or tooling, and are out of scope. Residual risk of a misordered or duplicate contact is bounded by showing 3 contacts with their roles and reasons rather than one answer. The coordinator makes the final choice. Add normalization later if the audit or pilot shows role-data gaps drive the misses. I cannot set what accuracy is acceptable for diplomatic outreach. That threshold is a policy call for the human owners, and I propose 90% as a pilot baseline only.

A single authoritative answer is a risk, and the fix is copy and a query clarification, both cheap. The country-level default no longer ranks by mission link, since mission linking is applied only when the user selects a context. That removes the 'whichever mission is most active' behaviour. The panel is relabelled 'suggested first contact', the ranking basis is always shown, and a fixed header says it is a country-level default and not topic-specific, with a prompt to select a mission or project. Reasons omit clauses tied to missions the viewer cannot see (see C2). A topic taxonomy stays out of scope, per A1, as it needs new schema and upkeep. Evidence that would justify adding topic handling later: coordinators reporting wrong-purpose outreach in the pilot.

challenges.challenge_text: A departed official with no inactive flag, but recently engaged, can still be suggested first, and a coordinator could send sensitive material to the wrong person.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The revision removes the noisy 180-day badge, which was the false-positive alert-fatigue risk. It shows the engagement date neutrally with an explicit 'does not confirm the person still holds this role' label. It also excludes contacts already flagged inactive. The remaining risk is a departure with no flag. That risk is bounded by the label, the display of 2 alternates, and the pilot criterion of zero known-departed suggestions. Fixing it fully needs coordinator data entry or a verification workflow, which is out of MVP scope. The proposer also sets a clear evidence trigger for adding a 'role ended' field later. Acceptable for an MVP.

challenges.challenge_text: A user with Country access but no Mission access could learn about a confidential mission or restricted engagement through reason text, alternates, the context selector, or last-engaged dates.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The revision adds the missing constraints. Queries run under the viewer's own permissions, not service-level access. Reason clauses, alternates, and selector entries that depend on invisible records are omitted. Default country-level ranking no longer uses mission links. An automated Country-without-Mission test must pass 100% before release. The proposer also handles the unverified-enforcement case: if access is only country-level, the panel falls back to contact details and role only. It treats any wider disclosure as a classification decision for a human owner and does not invent a policy. This adequately bounds the risk for an MVP. The release test will expose any row-level enforcement gap.

challenges.challenge_text: Free-text or inconsistent roles, duplicate contacts, and a presence-only 'valid' contact method could misorder suggestions. A coverage metric could also mask wrong recommendations.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The main gaps are closed. Role priority applies only to controlled-list values. The recorded role text is shown. The 'valid' label is now 'on file'. Coverage and correctness are separate metrics, with the pilot threshold raised to 90% and every miss root-caused. A pre-launch audit is a release gate with a list fallback. The defense of not adding normalization, deduplication, or bounce validation is reasonable for an MVP, because those are new tooling. Showing 3 contacts with their roles bounds the residual risk. The audit gate should have its numeric threshold fixed before launch, but that is a configuration detail, not an open design gap.

final_decision.feature_request: We need a better way to track who is the right person to contact in each country.
final_decision.executive_summary: v1 adds a 'Who to contact' panel on the country page. It shows one suggested first contact and up to two alternates, ranked by fixed, reproducible rules over existing Contact, Mission, Project and Engagement data. Each suggestion shows its ranking basis and a country-level disclaimer. The panel runs under the viewer's own permissions. The main trade-off was how far to trust engagement and role data for a diplomatic audience. It was settled by removing the 180-day stale badge and mission-based default ranking, by using role priority only where roles come from a controlled list, and by adding a pre-launch data-quality audit gate. It also leaves out new fields, tables, and verification workflows. All four challenged issues (C1-C4) ended ACCEPTED, no scope is pending, and no questions are escalated to humans. The pilot accuracy threshold and the audit gate's numeric cutoff still need to be fixed before launch.

Access: an automated test with a user who has Country access but no Mission access passes 100%. It confirms the panel shows no mission names, mission-derived reason text, mission-based ranking, or selector entries the user cannot see.

Pre-launch data-quality audit is run and published for all countries before release, and the role-priority step is disabled or the list fallback is used wherever role coverage is below the audit gate.
Zero new required fields or data-entry steps for Regional Coordinators, and zero new database tables in v1.
The panel loads in under 2 seconds at p95, and a user reaches a suggested contact within 2 clicks from the country page.
Every suggestion displays its ranking basis and the country-level disclaimer, and 100% of rankings are reproducible: identical data and permissions yield identical output.
The v1 feature ships within a single release cycle.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: 'Right person' means the best current contact for a given country, optionally narrowed to a mission or project; it is not a global directory or a per-topic expertise map.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: Challenged in C4 (a single authoritative answer could send a coordinator to the wrong person for a topic). The Proposer revised it by dropping mission-based ranking from the country default and adding a fixed disclaimer, and the Critic accepted.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: The existing Contact role, contact-detail and Engagement data is complete enough to rank contacts with simple deterministic rules, without any new fields being filled in.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: Challenged in C3 (role and contact data quality). The Proposer revised it with controlled-list-only role priority, 'on file' wording, a pre-launch audit gate and separate coverage and correctness criteria, and the Critic accepted.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Engagement history shows when we last interacted with a contact but cannot confirm they still hold the role; v1 shows that date neutrally and relies only on any inactive status already on the Contact record.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: Challenged in C1 (recency cannot detect departure). It was reworded so the last-engaged date is shown neutrally and only an existing inactive flag is used, with the stale badge removed, and the Critic accepted.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Existing Country/Mission access controls already determine who may see which contacts, so the new panel needs no separate permission model.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: Challenged in C2 (leaks through derived reasons and the selector). It was kept as worded and honoured by running queries under the viewer's permissions and omitting anything depending on records the viewer cannot see, and the Critic accepted.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Mission and Project affiliation, as already recorded on contacts, is the only context needed to tailor the recommendation in v1.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: Not challenged in the deliberation; accepted as proposed.
